title: Zedekiah's Fate and the Broken Covenant of Freedom

questions.question: When Nebuchadnezzar and all his army were fighting against Jerusalem, Jeremiah was given a message for King Zedekiah. What was he to tell Zedekiah his fate would be?
options: He would be given into the hand of the king of Babylon and speak to him face to face
He would die in battle on the walls of Jerusalem
He would escape to Egypt and die there
He would be killed by his own officials
questions.correctAnswer: He would be given into the hand of the king of Babylon and speak to him face to face
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:3 (ESV): "You shall not escape from his hand but shall surely be captured and delivered into his hand. You shall see the king of Babylon eye to eye and speak with him face to face."

questions.question: Did the Lord say Zedekiah would die by the sword?
options: No, he would die in peace.
Yes, he would be struck down in Riblah.
No, he would starve in prison.
Yes, his sons would kill him.
questions.correctAnswer: No, he would die in peace.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:4-5 (ESV): "You shall not die by the sword. You shall die in peace."

questions.question: "And as spices were burned for your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so people shall burn... for you and lament for you, saying, 'Alas, lord!'"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:5 (ESV): "so people shall burn spices for you and lament for you, saying, 'Alas, lord!'"

questions.question: At this time, which two fortified cities of Judah were the ONLY ones still holding out against the king of Babylon, besides Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:7 (ESV): "fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left, Lachish and Azekah, for these were the only fortified cities of Judah that remained."

questions.question: King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim what?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:8 (ESV): "after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to make a proclamation of liberty to them,"

questions.question: What kind of liberty was proclaimed?
options: That everyone should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female
That debtors would be forgiven their debts
That the gates would be opened to run away
That the prisoners of war would be released
questions.correctAnswer: That everyone should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:9 (ESV): "that everyone should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female, so that no one should enslave a Jew, his brother."

questions.question: After setting their slaves free, what did the officials and the people do later?
options: They turned around and took back the male and female slaves they had set free
They paid them wages to stay
They gave them land to farm
They forced them to fight on the wall
questions.correctAnswer: They turned around and took back the male and female slaves they had set free
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:11 (ESV): "But afterward they turned around and took back the male and female slaves they had set free, and brought them into subjection as slaves."

questions.question: The Lord reminded them of the covenant he made with their fathers when he brought them out of Egypt: "At the end of... years each of you must set free the fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you..."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:14 (ESV): "At the end of seven years each of you must set free the fellow Hebrew who has been sold to you and has served you six years;"

questions.question: "You recently repented and did what was right in my eyes by proclaiming liberty... but then you turned around and... my name when each of you took back his male and female slaves,"
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:15-16 (ESV): "but then you turned around and profaned my name when each of you took back his male and female slaves,"

questions.question: "Therefore, thus says the Lord: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming liberty... Behold, I proclaim to you liberty to the... , to pestilence, and to famine, declares the Lord."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 (ESV): "Behold, I proclaim to you liberty to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine, declares the Lord."

questions.question: "I will make you a... to all the kingdoms of the earth."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:17 (ESV): "I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth."

questions.question: What gruesome ritual had the leaders of Judah performed when making the covenant that they subsequently broke?
options: They cut a calf in two and passed between its parts
They poured blood on the altar
They swore by the temple treasury
They burned an offering to Molech
questions.correctAnswer: They cut a calf in two and passed between its parts
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:18 (ESV): "the covenant that they made before me, when they cut the calf in two and passed between its parts—"

questions.question: The men who transgressed the covenant and passed between the parts of the calf will be given into the hand of their enemies, and their dead bodies shall be food for what?
options: The birds of the air and the beasts of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: The birds of the air and the beasts of the earth
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:20 (ESV): "and their dead bodies shall be food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth."

questions.question: What did the Lord say about the army of the king of Babylon, which had currently withdrawn from Jerusalem?
options: "I will command, and they shall return to this city."
"They are waiting in Riblah to strike later."
questions.correctAnswer: "I will command, and they shall return to this city."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 (ESV): "Behold, I will command, declares the Lord, and will bring them back to this city. And they will fight against it and take it and burn it with fire."

questions.question: "And they will fight against it and take it and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without..."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 34:22 (ESV): "I will make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant."

key_verse_text: "Therefore, thus says the Lord: You have not obeyed me by proclaiming liberty, every one to his brother and to his neighbor; behold, I proclaim to you liberty to the sword, to pestilence, and to famine, declares the Lord. I will make you a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth."
